claims_extracted: BLS official release schedule lists Employment Situation releases at 08:30 AM.
The NBER paper studies real-time U.S. macroeconomic news in high-frequency foreign exchange markets.
The NBER abstract states that macro news surprises produce conditional mean jumps in high-frequency exchange-rate dynamics.
The repo implementation maps this mechanism to a first-Friday EURUSD M15 macro-announcement screen without claiming MT5 data equivalence or profitability.
limitations: The source supports macro-news price discovery, not a specific profitable EURUSD rule.
The current implementation approximates historical Employment Situation releases with first-Friday 08:30 ET timing and approximate U.S. DST conversion rather than a complete historical BLS calendar.
The screen uses OHLCV/tick-volume proxies only and does not observe announcement surprise magnitude, consensus, revisions, depth, or spread widening.
The current CSV is research data and does not prove FTMO terminal history equivalence.
disconfirming_relevance: Macro announcement effects can be absorbed within seconds, before M15 bars can enter without severe slippage.
NFP release dates can shift due to holidays or government disruptions, while this screen uses an approximation.
Direction may depend on surprise sign and risk regime, neither of which is observed here.
Announcement trading can be highly cost- and spread-sensitive.
